commitments.text: B.C. Hydro shall cause the Project to be designed, located, constructed and operated in accordance with the documents listed in Schedule A to this Project Approval Certificate, collectively comprising the proponent's Project Report, and without limiting the generality of the foregoing, B.C. Hydro shall cause the project to be designed, constructed and operated in accordance with the Mitigation and Compensation Plan, dated March 22, 1996.

B.C. Hydro shall complete an archaeological impact assessment under Section 7 of the Heritage Conservation Act of: a) the Waneta reservoir draw down zone between the minimum operating reservoir level and the uppermost 1.5 metres, when the opportunity arises; and b) the two terrace areas identified as having archaeological potential within the Waneta reservoir, described as 'B' and 'C' in Figure 2 of the Heritage Resource Impact Study, within two years of issuance of this Certificate. Upon completion of the archaeological impact assessment, B.C. Hydro shall implement measures for systematic data recovery of culturally significant deposits if warranted by the Archaeology Branch of the Ministry of Small Business, Tourism and Culture.

B.C. Hydro shall: a) prepare, in consultation with the Regional Director, Kootenay Region, MELP, the Department of Fisheries and Oceans (DFO) and CCRIFC, an environmental Management Plan (EMP) that addresses monitoring and control of construction impacts for the duration of the construction period, and includes a reclamation and revegetation plan for the upland storage and/or parking areas; b) submit the EMP to the Comptroller of Water Rights for approval prior to the Comptroller of Water Rights granting leave to construct Unit 4; and c) implement the approved EMP to the satisfaction of the Engineer under the Water Act.

B.C. Hydro, in consultation with, and to the satisfaction of the Regional Director, Kootenay Region, MELP and the Area Chief, Eastern B.C. Habitat Unit, DFO, shall retain the services of a qualified environmental inspector to monitor construction of the Project to ensure compliance with the EMP. The inspector shall report to the Project construction manager, and have the authority to cease activities of the Project to prevent environmental degradation. The terms of reference for the inspector shall be set out in the EMP.

B.C. Hydro shall, prior to installation of Unit 4: a) develop, in consultation with the CCRIFC and its member First Nations, a plan to: i) achieve equity training and employment consistent with the terms of the agreement between the Columbia Hydro Constructors and the Allied Hydro Council; and ii) identify economic development and contracting opportunities for First Nations for the Seven Mile Unit 4 Project.

B.C. Hydro shall, prior to installation of Unit 4: b) contribute $30,000 to CCRIFC to enable its member First Nations to develop an information base which can be used to deal with future projects in the vicinity of the Seven Mile Dam and their potential impacts on traditional uses.

B.C. Hydro shall impose, as a condition of employment during the construction period, a ban on the use of the campground at the B.C. Hydro Buckley Recreation site as semipermanent or permanent accommodation by construction workers. If, in the reasonable opinion of the Regional District of Kootenay Boundary, increased use by construction workers of the B.C. Hydro Buckley Recreation site becomes a problem, B.C. Hydro shall spend up to $50,000, during the Seven Mile Unit 4 construction period, to provide temporary informal public camping facilities at other sites along the Seven Mile Reservoir, or at off-site locations as may be requested by the Regional District of Kootenay Boundary in consultation with B.C. Parks.

B.C. Hydro shall, in consultation with the public, the Regional District of Kootenay Boundary, MELP, and the Ministry of Transportation and Highways, prepare a Traffic Management Plan for review and approval by the Ministry of Transportation and Highways, prior to commencement of construction, to address potential traffic impacts on wildlife mortality, recreational users, and local users on the Waneta/Nelway road.

B.C. Hydro shall comply with the requirements of the Fisheries Act (Canada), and obtain any and all lawful authorizations of the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans, and in particular, shall: a) adhere to the Authorization for Works or Undertakings affecting Fish Habitat and for Destruction of Fish for Seven Mile Unit 4; and b) carry out or cause to be carried out the fish habitat compensation program described in the Seven Mile Unit 4 Habitat Compensation Agreement, dated March 22, 1996, between the Minister of Fisheries and Oceans and B.C. Hydro.

Condition 1 is amended by deleting "Seven Mile Unit 4 Mitigation and Compensation Plan, dated March 22, 1996" and substituting therefore the following "Seven Mile Unit 4 Mitigation and Compensation Plan, revised 2001, and the South Salmo Stream Fertilization Program (2001)".
